players.product: BlueBird Block 2 direct-to-cell satellites (custom AST5000 ASIC) and MNO gateway equipment

quarterly_data.signal: AST 10-K: 2025 total revenues were $70,918 thousand - products revenues of $44.4 million from sales of gateway equipment and software to MNOs and services revenues of $26.5 million mainly from performance obligations under agreements with the U.S. Government (directly as a prime contractor or through prime contractors); net loss attributable to common stockholders was $341.9 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenues $70,918 thousand; products $44.4 million; services $26.5 million; net loss $341.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: AST 10-K: remaining performance obligations were approximately $1.2 billion at December 31, 2025 (approximately 9.0% expected within 12 months) and contract liabilities $227.0 million; under its ten-year agreement STC committed to a prepayment of $175.0 million during 2025 (received net of withholding taxes), and Verizon's $45.0 million commercial prepayment is only contingent on regulatory approvals for the SpaceMobile Service; minimum commitments for future launches were approximately $250.0 - $325.0 million.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO approximately $1.2 billion (9.0% within 12 months); STC prepayment $175.0 million; Verizon $45.0 million; launch commitments $250.0 - $325.0 million

quarterly_data.signal: AST 10-K: AST owns the IP and controls manufacturing, internally or through contract manufacturers, for approximately 95% of the sub-systems in its Block 2 satellites; it has completed investments for capacity to assemble, integrate and test up to six Block 2 satellites per month, completed fully assembled microns for up to 28 BB satellites, and BB8 to BB29 are in production and integration. Launch agreements with multiple providers cover over 60 Block 2 satellites, with approximately 45 to 60 Block 2 satellites planned by the end of 2026 at a cadence of one launch approximately every one to two months; global footprint approximately 450,000 square feet and approximately 1,126 employees.
quarterly_data.figure: 95% of sub-systems; up to six satellites per month; microns for 28 satellites; 45 to 60 Block 2 by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: AST 10-K: spectrum and regulatory - AST has executed lease agreements with Verizon and AT&T and a similar agreement with FirstNet, and in August 2025 the FCC authorized 20 additional satellites; AST acquired an entity holding S-Band ITU priority rights (1980-2010 MHz and 2170-2200 MHz) on September 25, 2025, expected to add up to 60 MHz of mid-band satellite spectrum; AST pays the Crown Castle Annual Payment for up to 5 MHz of 1670-1675 MHz spectrum. For the Ligado transaction, Inmarsat filed a New York State action in December 2025 instead of providing regulatory support; in January 2026 the Bankruptcy Court ordered Inmarsat to comply, and Inmarsat appealed.
quarterly_data.figure: 20 additional satellites; up to 60 MHz S-band; up to 5 MHz of 1670-1675 MHz

quarterly_data.signal: AST 10-K: on July 7, 2025 AST and Vodafone agreed to create SatCo, a jointly-owned European satellite service business headquartered in Luxembourg to exclusively distribute AST's broadband satellite services to MNOs in European markets, which is also expected to deploy a small network of earth stations; AST recognized $2.1 million of revenue from gateway equipment sales to SatCo in 2025.
